transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-03-23 15:00 UTC | Duration: 58m | Attendees: Liam, Priya, Marcos (Redwood) — Aisha, Kenji, Sofia, Tommy (HorizonStack)

Summary: Quick sync to validate marketplace packaging, VPC connector patterns, and security requirements before pilot.

[00:00] Liam Chen: Hey everyone thanks for joining, I think we have about an hour. Quick intros?
[00:10] Aisha Bello: Hi yes Aisha here, Head of Cloud Partnerships at HorizonStack. We own the go-to-market for marketplace listings.
[00:18] Kenji Ito: Kenji, platform eng. I'll be hands-on for the network pieces.
[00:22] Sofia Ruiz: Sofia, security. I'll review the KMS and audit expectations.
[00:27] Marcos Alvarez: Marcos from Redwood, I help with on-prem connectors and runbooks.
[00:31] Priya Desai: Priya, SE — I'll own benching and perf validation.
[00:36] Tommy Park: Tommy, DevOps. I do the packaging and automation.

[02:05] Liam: Cool, today's agenda — one, marketplace listing artifact & assets; two, connectivity options (VPC peering vs onprem connector); three, security: KMS, audit logs, SSO; four, pilot success criteria and timeline. Anything to add?
[02:18] Aisha: Sounds good — also want clarity on billing model for the listing (consumption vs reserved).
[02:24] Liam: We'll cover that briefly but finance follow-up doc will come after.

[04:10] Kenji: On connectivity, our main constraint is we can't open broad egress from the customer's on-prem environment. We prefer a reverse-connector or a private link. What's Redwood's recommended pattern?
[04:25] Priya: For most partners we support three patterns: 1) Direct VPC peering or PrivateLink to Redwood Dedicated endpoints; 2) On-prem agent that establishes an outbound mTLS tunnel to Redwood Private control plane; 3) Hybrid with an edge connector in customer's cloud account. Each has tradeoffs.
[04:45] Kenji: Right, the outbound-only approach is better for us, less firewall changes.
[04:50] Marcos: The outbound agent is what we call the Private Connector — it initiates TLS to Redwood control, authenticates with certs; it can multiplex inference traffic to a nearby region. We documented token encryption and KMS integration in the runbook (link: confluence/hzst/redwood-connector).

[06:30] Sofia: On KMS — are keys customer-managed? We need envelope encryption and separation of duties. Also audit trails must show key usage per request.
[06:41] Priya: Yes we support Customer-Managed Keys (CMK) via standard KMS integrations — AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and a KMIP adapter for on-prem HSMs. Key usage logs are emitted to the audit pipeline, we can produce per-request metadata including key id, model id, request id. Note: some of these fields may be truncated in the streaming logs depending on throughput.
[07:12] Sofia: Truncated logs are a no-go for us, we need full auditability for certain regulated customers. Is there a retention SLA?
[07:20] Marcos: We have configurable retention settings; for Private deployments retention can be pushed to the customer's log sink (S3/Blob) and we can increase retention. We'll include this in the security artifact.

[09:05] Tommy: Packaging question — the marketplace requires a single VM image or container with the connector plus docs. How opinionated is Redwood about the packaging?
[09:16] Liam: We try to be flexible. For Azure Marketplace we provide both a VM/ARM template and a containerized Helm chart for AKS/EKS. For on-prem we can provide an OVA or a Docker compose reference. The key is the config: certs, bootstrap tokens, and allowed CIDRs.

[11:30] Aisha: For listing description — we need a short blurb, feature bullets, and verified performance numbers. Can Redwood supply a small verified benchmark and a pack of screenshots?
[11:41] Priya: Yes, we'll provide a verified bench run with p50/p95/p99 for the model family you choose. We can also provide sample dashboards from Redwood Console for the marketplace listing.

[13:50] Kenji: About benching — can we run with our prompt set? We have a mix of short queries and long-turn dialogs. Throughput matters because we multi-tenant.
[14:05] Priya: Absolutely. Best is you provide a representative prompt corpus and we run three scenarios: short (<=64 tokens), medium (<=512), long (>=1024). We'll capture tokens/sec and latency percentiles. Note: quantization profiles may change latency.

[16:40] Sofia: Security question: SSO and RBAC. We need our customers to authenticate via their IdP; marketplace listing must not force separate accounts.
[16:52] Marcos: Our Private control plane supports SAML 2.0/ OIDC federation. For Dedicated and Private we can federate into your IdP and map groups to RBAC roles. We'll share a mapping doc.

[18:30] Aisha: Another commercial question — on billing, can we have co-billing or separate metered billing for customers that come through HorizonStack listing?
[18:45] Liam: Both are possible — co-billing via marketplace or referral tracking. We'll outline options in the pricing template.

[20:10] Kenji: Network specifics — what source IPs do we need to allow in the firewall for outbound connector?
[20:18] Marcos: We'll provide a small set of egress endpoints per region. For air-gapped customers we can support a proxy or local inference nodes. We'll list IP ranges in the packaging checklist.

[22:00] Tommy: For the on-prem agent, what's the upgrade mechanism? We need unattended upgrades and a rollback plan.
[22:09] Priya: The agent supports automatic rolling upgrades with a canary flag. We ship a reconciliation controller that ensures desired version; rollback uses previous image. We'll include the playbook for canary rollback.

[24:50] Sofia: About data residency — some customers require that embedding requests not leave EU. Can Redwood pin inference to a region inside their control?
[25:04] Marcos: For Dedicated and Private yes. Hosted Redwood API can be region pinned too but if you need strict on-premality, Private deployment is the path. We can route by policy to the customer's dedicated cluster in eu-west-1.

[27:30] Kenji: Ok, pilot timeline — we want a small pilot with three internal accounts, run over two weeks. Success criteria: throughput >= X tokens/sec, p95 latency < 300ms for short prompts, no audit gaps.
[27:46] Priya: Sounds reasonable. We'll propose concrete numbers after we see your prompt corpus.

[29:10] Aisha: Any blockers on marketplace certification? Some marketplaces require security attestations and a third-party vulnerability scan.
[29:22] Liam: We can provide our SOC2 Type II report and a standard vulnerability scan. For Azure Marketplace there is a separate certification but we've done it with other partners — it usually takes 2-4 weeks.

[31:50] Kenji: On the subject of latency SLOs — what mechanisms do you have for graceful degradation? If a model is overloaded what happens?
[32:01] Priya: We have smart routing and compatible fallbacks — if a large LLM variant is saturated we route to quantized variant or smaller model, and we expose headers with the model variant. There's also autoscaling if you're on dedicated pools, and a circuit-breaker to avoid cascading failures.

[34:40] Tommy: For the listing we want to include a link to a quickstart repo. Do you have a sample repo we can fork?
[34:49] Marcos: Yes — we'll share a public quickstart with Helm charts and an example connector config. We'll add a HorizonStack-specific example.

[36:20] Sofia: A couple of nitty-gritty items: are logs redacted for PII by default? How do you handle prompt logging and retention?
[36:33] Priya: By default we store prompts and responses for debugging for a short window, customers can opt-out or configure redaction rules and forward only metadata. For Private deployments the data residencies are controlled by the customer; you can disable prompt retention entirely.

[38:00] Aisha: Okay let's recap next steps quickly. Liam?
[38:06] Liam: We'll share: 1) marketplace listing draft, 2) packaging checklist + IP ranges, 3) bench plan template. HorizonStack will share network diagram and prompt corpus. SE will begin bench run and security will exchange SOC2/attestation docs.

[40:10] Kenji: Quick follow — is there a formal support SLA during pilot? We need fast response for infra issues.
[40:20] Liam: Pilot support included, we'll assign an onboarding CSM and have SE on-call for bench windows. For production we can negotiate SLA add-on.

[42:00] Marcos: I want to call out one gotcha we see — KV cache reuse across tenants can leak if not namespaced. If you use a shared cache pattern be sure to namespace per-account; we'll provide config examples.
[42:15] Kenji: Good to know — we'll audit our cache layer.

[44:05] Tommy: Anything in the marketplace requirements specific to telemetry or metadata we should embed?
[44:15] Liam: Marketplaces like to see a short onboarding flow and observability screenshots. They don't typically require extended telemetry beyond errors/usage, but we can include a short doc showing per-tenant cost breakdown and latency heatmaps.

[46:30] Sofia: For the security questionnaire, I'll expect answers on key rotation policy, MFA for admin accounts, and penetration test cadence.
[46:40] Marcos: We'll populate those fields in the security artifact. Also note we have a standard pen-test report we can share if needed.

[48:20] Priya: On benchmarks — small note: tokenization differences across model families can affect tokens/sec. We'll normalize using your sample prompts.
[48:31] Kenji: Good. Also, for long prompts we may want KV-cache prefetching. Does Redwood support prefix caching?
[48:42] Priya: Yes we have prefix/KV cache features for persistent contexts. We can demo caching performance in the bench run.

[50:10] Aisha: Let's lock dates: can we aim to have the marketplace draft by next Friday?
[50:18] Liam: Yes — I'll send the draft by 2026-03-27.

[51:40] Sofia: One more question — are there any hard limits on model size for the on-prem connector?
[51:50] Marcos: The connector proxies to whatever cluster you deploy — if you want the largest LLM you need matching GPU capacity on the customer's cluster or a Dedicated pool. For constrained on-prem nodes we recommend quantized 8-bit variants.

[53:20] Kenji: Ok thanks — anything else?
[53:25] Tommy: Nothing from me.
[53:28] Aisha: All good. Thanks team.

[55:00] Liam: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the artifacts and schedule the UAT kickoff.
[55:07] Marcos: I'll draft the canary rollback playbook.
[55:12] Priya: I'll prep the bench plan.

[56:00] Meeting ended.

Notes: Transcript includes occasional mis-hearings by auto transcribe; some product names abbreviated. Links referenced: confluence/hzst/redwood-connector, github.com/redwood/marketplace-quickstart
